messages:
Maria G.: Helix GPU pool in eu-central finished provisioning. Kicking off the post-provision validation checklist here so we have a single place to track. Quick note: noticed NIC offload flaps on 3 nodes during initial perf runs. Posting raw results below.

Kevin L.: Nice — can you paste the checklist you're following?

Maria G.: Checklist I'm using (short):
```
1) Basic cluster health: `kubectl get nodes,pods -A` and node disk/mem checks
2) Network sanity: ping, iperf between nodes, check NIC driver logs
3) Perf smoke: run small/medium/large batch latency profiles (p50,p95,p99)
4) SLO gates: p50<50ms, p95<150ms, p99<300ms (for this pool)
5) Cost/throughput sanity: expected tokens/sec vs actual, check batching
6) Alerts & rollback: verify alert thresholds and rollback plan in calendar
```

infra-bot: smoke-checker started against `helix-gpu-pool` (run id: sc-193876). Results will post when finished.

Ryan H.: Ran perf smoke earlier: p50 21ms, p95 120ms, p99 260ms overall. However helix-3, helix-8, helix-11 showed p99 ~240ms for baseline tests and some NIC reset logs (see journalctl).

Maria G.: Thanks Ryan. Marking helix-3/8/11 as quarantine candidates. I'll patch NIC driver on a canary node first. Current impact: after removing those 3 nodes from traffic, pool p99 drops to ~110ms.

Kevin L.: On cost — current burn is ~2.4x our expected on-demand estimate because batching is still at conservative params. I suggest enabling burst batching policy and prefix caching for this pool once SLOs are stable. I'll open a PR for batching config afterwards.

SRE-Oncall: Anything blocking handoff to SRE? We need the health checks and SLO gates green, cost gating acknowledged, and rollback steps documented. Current thresholds we require: p50<50ms, p95<150ms, p99<300ms.

Maria G.: Current numbers (with quarantined nodes): p50=21ms, p95=120ms, p99=110ms. Health checks: kube pods all Ready, disk/mem normal. Network: basic iperf shows <1ms intra-rack, inter-rack ~2-4ms, but NIC error rate on quarantined nodes ~0.6%. Will run NIC driver canary tonight and revalidate.

Kevin L.: Linking the runbook/notes: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/helix-gpu-post-provision (internal). Also we should gate cost alert at 1.5x expected until batching PR is merged.

Ryan H.: Commands I ran for reproducibility:
```
./perf_check --nodes helix-* --batch 8 --seq 256 --report /tmp/helix-perf.json
ssh ops@helix-3 'journalctl -u nic-driver | tail -n 200'
kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=helix-metrics -o wide
```

Maria G.: OK — plan: 1) Canaried NIC driver patch on helix-8 tonight (22:00 UTC), 2) monitor for 2 hours, 3) if green, roll to helix-3/11, 4) re-run perf checks and confirm SLOs. Handoff conditions: health checks green, SLO gates met, cost gating acknowledged, alerts in place, and rollback steps in calendar invite. If everyone :thumbsup: we schedule an SRE handoff tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

Kevin L.: :thumbsup: Please also enable prefix cache and the dynamic burst batching for this pool in the same window — will reduce token cost and improve p99 tail. I'll have the PR ready.

SRE-Oncall: Agreed. Add me to the change window invite and add a short alert: NIC driver error rate >0.5% -> pager. Also include a dashboard link in the invite.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy helix-nic-driver v2.1 initiated by Maria G. Monitoring hooks enabled. (deploy id: dpl-193876-helix)

Maria G.: Added alerts and calendar invite, included dashboard + rollback steps. Will post canary outcomes here. Thanks all — will update after the 2hr canary. --Maria

Ryan H.: I'll watch logs during canary and stand by to abort if NIC errors spike.

infra-bot: smoke-checker queued follow-up run for after canary (run id: sc-193876-2).
